description: issue #679 (SP7): the declaration-slot rule covers struct CONSTRUCTORS as well as procedures, so with `sprites` active `struct tell`/`struct ask`/`struct each` each raise `ol-reserved-word` at the struct-name token. `struct` is one of the grammar's four declaration slots (spec/grammar.md:382), which is why this fixture is unaffected by maintainer ruling #833. Scope note, twice corrected: when this fixture was written the `variables` third of spec/turtles-and-sprites.md:154's sentence was not diagnosed (`:tell = 1` checked clean); Epic-Gate finding B3 took that up as issue #739, which made it raise; ruling #833 then reversed #739 and made binding free again, permanently -- spec/grammar.md:386 now makes accepting any name in a binding position a normative MUST, and spec/grammar.md:408 says what a profile decides is whether a name WORKS, never whether a program may declare it. The sibling fixture reserved-bindings-with-sprites pins that reversal; realigning the profile document's older wording is issue #855. This fixture owns the struct-constructor case, which is a declaration and still collides. Issue #838 dropped the `namespace` param (spec/error-model.md:125) and made the built-in half of the struct check unconditional, so `struct tell` would now raise even Core-only -- what still needs `sprites` here is `tell` being a built-in name at all, which is #841's to retire.

diagnostics.message: tell is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
ask is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
each is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
